Widening only the open-denominator branch to 21 pushes this expression toward that stronger pattern.

A bare RANK of an unsmoothed quarterly field is exposed to point-in-time report-date staggering noise across names. Rule 2's guidance to use quarter-scale (21d+) windows on fundamentals applies here even without an explicit delta: wrapping $roa in a 21d mean smooths that noise while leaving the RANK wrapper untouched.

Its same-shape sibling at window 63 (parent 5dd286d81a38617b) scores far lower (1.952), and this round's strongest accept used a 5d window on this exact dollar_volume ratio — the 10d window is the one lever unsupported by any diagnostic, so shorten it to match the window shown to work best for this shape.
A 10-day rolling correlation is a statistically noisy, high-variance estimator; lengthening to 21 gives a materially more stable correlation estimate while leaving both input series untouched.

Per rule 2's quarter-scale-window guidance, smoothing only $leverage over 21d reduces that noise without touching the margin*turnover term.

A flat 21d average weights a stale 3-week-old liquidity reading equally with today's; swapping the smoothing operator to EMA emphasizes recent dollar volume while keeping field and window fixed, and avoids introducing a second raw dollar_volume window that rule 3 flags as redundant.

This is the weakest accept in the range-ratio family (1.952, versus 3.481 for the same shape at a shorter window with a dollar_volume denominator) — the 63d window is the clear outlier. Shortening it to 21 moves toward the window scale shown to perform better for this shape.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.

  1. Coverage failures cluster on fundamental fields (roa, leverage, operating_margin, asset_turnover) pushed through long transforms (delta/argmax/mean at 126-252d) — quarterly reporting gaps compound at long horizons, landing at 0.82-0.88 four times this round.   2. Cheap-screen failures were short-window (5d) deltas on slow-moving fundamentals (accrual_gap, operating_margin) — the signal itself is too weak (t 0.55-0.65) because these fields barely move day to day, not because the expression is costly. Use quarter-scale windows (21d+) when differencing fundamentals.
  3. Dollar_volume smoothed at nearby windows (21d vs 63d) is redundant and trips correlation when both appear as separate terms in one expression. Space smoothing windows further apart or make one a transform of the other rather than two raw levels.

A genuinely different normalization is needed, not reshuffled inputs.

  7. Resubmitting a raw fundamental field alongside its already-archived RANK() form is a guaranteed correlation failure (rho=1.0). Check whether a ranked version of a field is already archived before proposing the raw field.
  8. This round's strongest accept (fitness 3.96) contrasted the same ratio shape at two different smoothing windows and spread the ranks, while the weakest accept (0.107) was a generic reversal-rank times roa-rank fusion that barely survived. Favor same-shape/different-window spreads over generic two-factor multiplicative fusions.
